Observations: The first-layer weights show strong structure almost entirely in channels 1 (moving objects) and 4 (previous frame), with a smaller but very consistent set in channel 0 (agent). Channel 0 appears only in column 1, at rows such as 1, 2, 6, 7, 8: e.g. unit 1 has (r2,c1,ch0) â3.588; unit 11 has (r1,c1,ch0) 2.697; unit 21 has (r8,c1,ch0) 2.358. This indicates the agentâs horizontal position is fixed at the left playable column and it moves vertically. Channel 1 is spread across many columns and rows, e.g. unit 6 has (r5,c4,ch1) 4.754; unit 3 has (r2,c8,ch1) 1.616; unit 12 has (r4,c6,ch1) 3.170. This suggests moving objects traverse the grid, including near the right side. Channel 4 is also widespread, consistent with using the previous frame to infer motion. Crucially, there are no top-8 connections to channel 2 (reward targets) or channel 3 (obstacles), implying the game has no separate reward-target cells and no internal obstacles beyond the border.

Reasoning: The fixed left-column agent strongly suggests a paddle on the left side that moves vertically. The moving objects spread across the grid fit a ball and an opponent paddle on the right. The absence of reward targets and internal obstacles rules out games like Breakout, Space Invaders, Asterix, Seaquest, Pac-Man, and Sokoban. Freeway is less likely because its agent is typically free to move horizontally or is centered, whereas here the agent is locked to column 1. The pattern is exactly that of Pong: left paddle controlled by the agent, ball and right paddle as moving objects, reward when the ball passes the opponent.

Game: Pong

Description: The agent controls the left paddle and moves it up or down to hit the ball. Reward is given when the ball gets past the opponentâs right-side paddle.

Confidence: 90%
